plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A hybrid flowering cherry tree that produces clouds of delicate, five-petaled blossoms before its leaves emerge. The flowers are pale pink fading to nearly white and have a faint almond scent.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The 3,000 cherry trees given by Tokyo to Washington D.C. in 1912 were mostly Yoshino cherries, and the National Cherry Blossom Festival celebrates their peak bloom each spring.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A perennial bulb with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and gray-green strap-like leaves. The native wild form is smaller and more delicate than cultivated daffodils, with pale outer petals and a deeper yellow trumpet.
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain, in woodlands and meadows; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids that make it toxic, which is why deer and rodents generally leave it alone. Galantamine, a compound from related Amaryllidaceae plants, is used in Alzheimer's medication.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large deciduous tree with spectacular goblet-shaped flowers up to 30 cm across that open on bare branches. The blooms are rich pink to deep rose and make a dramatic display in early spring.
plants.location: Himalayan foothills of Nepal, Bhutan, and northeast India; cultivated in mild gardens in the UK, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Campbell's magnolia can take 20 to 30 years from seed to produce its first flowers, so patient gardeners are rewarded with one of the most dramatic blooms in the plant world.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Although famous for autumn blooms in the north, many Southern Hemisphere gardens see related bulbs such as Nerine and Amaryllis belladonna flowering in March and April. Amaryllis belladonna produces tall bare stems topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, and California
plants.funFact: Amaryllis belladonna is nicknamed the naked lady because its flowers appear on bare stems after the leaves have died back, and its flowers emerge in late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere.
